title: Parameter signature protocol for partial/streamed tool calls and humanized error taxonomy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a parameter signature format and runtime protocol that supports partial/streamed tool/function invocation, incremental validation, backwards-compatible legacy shims, and human-friendly error messages. This ticket covers the JSON schema extension, runtime validation modes, error code taxonomy, example messages, telemetry hooks, and a migration plan for existing tool manifests.
acceptance_criteria: A compact JSON schema extension (v1) exists that allows fields to be marked with 'partial' semantics for streaming inputs.
Runtime can accept streaming parameter payloads and run incremental validation without blocking full response generation.
Validation modes (strict, permissive, repair) are implemented and configurable per route/model and produce standardized error codes.
A mapping shim converts common legacy parameter names to new schema fields for backward compatibility (configurable per tool).
Error messages surface actionable repair suggestions and a short human-friendly summary with a unique error code for telemetry.
E2E tests validating streaming scenarios, partial failures, and graceful degradation are added to CI.
Docs and an example authoring guide for tool authors (including snippet for streaming chat completion calls) are published in the dev docs repo.
implementation_notes: Schema extension: add top-level properties 'streamable': boolean, 'partial_validation': enum{none, prefix, incremental}, and 'repair_hint': string to parameter definitions.

Runtime flow: accept an initial schema-validated header, then accept incremental parameter chunks (JSON-lines); run incremental validators on each chunk and emit inline validation events in the response stream.

Validation modes: strict -> reject first violation (400), permissive -> accept & emit warning code (V01) and try to coerce, repair -> attempt automatic fixes (type casts, trim whitespace, default fills) and emit repair events (R02).
Compatibility shim: allow 'legacy_field_map' in tool manifest that maps old names to new canonical names and mark deprecated aliases with TTL in days.
Telemetry: emit metrics 'param.validation.failures', 'param.validation.repairs', 'param.stream.length', and include error_code and route_id in spans.
Rollout: feature-flagged per-customer and per-route; default off for existing public hosted tools until migration window completes.
Security: ensure streaming chunks are size-limited and rate-limited; validate no executable content in 'repair_hint' or messages to avoid injection into logs or UIs.
decisions: Use a lightweight schema extension (no full draft-7 changes) to reduce authoring friction and avoid breaking existing validators.
Expose three validation modes (strict, permissive, repair) rather than a boolean flag to give fine-grained control to platform teams and customers.
Emit validation events inline in the response stream so callers can react in real time (e.g., prompt the user for missing fields) rather than returning a single error after completion.
Implement compatibility shim server-side to avoid forcing all tool authors to update manifests at once.
Human-friendly error messages will include a 6-character error code prefix 'PV' (parameter validation) followed by numeric type and a short slug, e.g. 'PV-104-missing-address'.
open_questions: Should repair-mode changes be applied silently by default or require explicit acknowledgement from the caller via a response flag?
What is the canonical format for inline validation events in the streaming protocol (JSON-lines with 'event_type' vs. SSE)?
How do we surface repaired parameter values in tracing without leaking sensitive user data?
What default TTL for deprecated legacy aliases is reasonable (30d, 90d, 180d)?
test_plan: Unit tests for schema parser: validation of 'streamable' and 'partial_validation' flags and error on unknown values.
Integration tests simulating chunked parameter sends with missing middle chunks and ensuring incremental validators emit expected events.
Fuzz tests to ensure malformed chunk sequences don't cause runtime panics or OOM conditions.
E2E tests for permissive/repair/strict modes verifying telemetry and returned messages for each failure type.
Manual UX review with a design PR demonstrating how streaming validation events are shown in the console for tool authors.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement schema extension and compatibility shim; add validation-mode config to route settings behind flag.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Enable repair mode for internal tools and run synthetic traffic to measure repair rate and false positives.
Phase 3 (4 weeks): Offer opt-in for customer tools with a migration checklist and automatic alias mapping suggestions in Console.
Phase 4 (8 weeks): Default permissive mode for newly created tools; deprecation notices for legacy aliases with analytics showing usage per alias.
Phase 5 (after migration window): Switch default to strict for new routes and retire shim for aliases with no usage.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after spike that showed ~12% of long-form tool calls include user-supplied attachments that arrive progressively. We need incremental validation to avoid blocking generation while waiting for full payload.
